features.notes: Missing Mode becomes explicit OneWay. Existing binding engine handles the resulting markup; Mode=Default requires explicit review.
Explicit for_winui_theme policy maps to live DynamicResource lookup. Ported dictionaries and theme scopes must be supplied; this is not proof of all WinUI theme semantics.

Rejected by default. Explicit PropertyPathsWithExplicitLifecycle policy preserves typed root/named-element sources, typed template item scopes, OneTime default, OneWay/TwoWay tracking, TextBox LostFocus writeback and explicit Initialize/Update/StopTracking lifecycle. Functions, events, casts, indexers, phased and deferred loading remain diagnosed. This is not complete compiled-binding parity.
Application namespace mappings rewrite class identity explicitly. C# code-behind still requires a Rust port.

Type references follow explicit alias mappings. In the opt-in property-path x:Bind policy, each template instance validates its source item against its resolved native data type. Other compiled/deferred expression contracts remain unsupported.
Deferred creation and named-element lifetime require implementation; the migration pass reports the directive.
Namescope spelling is preserved; named field/code-behind creation remains owned by the normal XAML compiler.
Phased rendering lifecycle is not implemented by renaming this directive.

meaning: Audited syntax adaptations and explicit rejections, separate from behavior.
